answer:
Tesla is facing major shifts, including plans to phase out the Cybertruck, declining profits, stock drops, and vehicle controversies:

* **Cybertruck Phase-Out:** CEO Elon Musk announced that Tesla will wind down production of the polarizing Cybertruck at its Texas plant—with production paring back from mid-2027 and ending next year—to free up capacity for the Cybercab robotaxi [1, 2, 3, 6, 7].
* **Cybertruck Struggles:** The stainless-steel pickup struggled with poor sales across few markets, quality-control problems, multiple voluntary recalls, and recent cancellations of its planned launches in Australia and New Zealand [3, 4, 9, 10, 11, 15].
* **Financial and Stock Drop:** Tesla profits dropped 43% in the third quarter [16], and its stock plummeted following the midterms amid investor concerns over a potential Tesla-SpaceX merger and a combined market cap loss [12, 13].
* **Roadster Uncertainty:** Tesla stated it "cannot guarantee" that Roadster reservation holders will ever receive a car [17], despite a debut appearance showcasing a sub-one-second 0–60 MPH time [19].
* **Other Incidents:** Recent headlines also note a Tesla Semi fire on I-880 [14] and an NHTSA petition alleging that Tesla robotaxis have blown through school zones [20].
